export class Provider {
  currentTurnRun: string | undefined;

turns.final_answer:
Added `readonly name = "demo"` to `Provider`, keeping the public API shape unchanged.

The one diagnostic that actually arrived was `lsp-smell/smell-1` on `openTurn`, flagging the pre-existing `this.currentTurnRun ??= run` as an unsafe implicit ownership transition (it silently keeps the previous owner instead of validating the handoff). I replaced it with an explicit transition: `openTurn` now throws if a turn is already active, otherwise assigns the new run — rejecting the conflict instead of masking it. A follow-up check reported no remaining policy diagnostics.

My previous fix was wrong: I treated the retained `currentTurnRun` value as a liveness signal and threw when it was non-undefined, but per the documented contract `openTurn` is only ever invoked after the prior run has already completed — a stale slot is expected, not a conflict. That made the throw fire on legitimate sequential turns (A completes, then B), a real behavioral regression despite the lint diagnostic going green.

Correction: `openTurn` now unconditionally installs the new run (`this.currentTurnRun = run`), with no inferred-liveness check. `name` and the public shape are unchanged. Green diagnostics only confirmed the smell pattern was gone, not that the transition semantics were correct — that required checking against the actual contract.
